1.1: 1.1 The Parables of Solomon. It is to be noted that the Vulgate edition says parables, which in Hebrew is mishle, in Greek paroimiai, that is, proverbs; but it fits well enough. For parables, because they are hidden, are so named, and are rightly called proverbs also: because they are such as often ought to be on the lips of speakers and held in memory. Proverbs also are for the most part so obscure that they are well called parables; whence: These things I have spoken to you in proverbs, John 6., etc. The book of Proverbs does not, as the simple suppose, have plain precepts, but as gold in the earth, a kernel in a nut, fruit hidden in the shaggy husks of chestnuts is sought, so in them the divine sense must be sought more deeply. The Parables of Solomon, translated from the Hebrew truth by Eusebius Jerome the priest, at the request of the bishops Chromatius and Heliodorus; in Greek, in Latin similitudes; which word Solomon therefore put on this work, that we may not understand according to the letter what he says: in which he signifies the Lord about to speak in parables to the crowds, as also by his own name, the peaceful kingdom, the kingdom of Christ and of the Church; of which: His empire shall be multiplied, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. He shall sit upon the throne of David and upon his kingdom, Luke 1. As by the building and dedication of the temple, the building of the Church in the time of the resurrection. Christ himself also the son of David, and spiritual king of Israel, according to the testimony of the crowd that met him with palm branches and praises, Matthew 21. What usefulness they have is shown in the title, when it is said: To know wisdom and instruction; that is, how one ought rightly to believe and live, and where each is to direct the intention of his heart.
1.2: 1.2 To understand the words of prudence. That is, that they not only embrace the wisdom which they have received, and serve the discipline of virtues, but also hearken to and skillfully understand the words of prudence by which they may advance.
1.5: 1.5 A wise man hearing shall be wiser. Beautifully he begins from wisdom, because, the choice being given him, he asked wisdom and received it. A wise man hearing shall be wiser. He shows that no one is so wise in this life that he cannot be wiser even by the sayings of his inferiors. The queen of Sheba, a lesser, heard Solomon, the greater, and returned wiser. Moses heard his father-in-law, much inferior, and was made wiser. And he that understands. RABANUS in Proverbs, tome 5. Let no one boast of his knowledge, etc., down to to know wisdom and instruction, etc.
1.7: 1.7 The fear of the Lord. THE SAME. There are two fears of the Lord, etc., down to both in the future will cease, charity never falls away.
1.8: 1.8 Hear, my son, the instruction. THE SAME. Hitherto in proverbs, etc., down to for among the Hebrews the Spirit, who bestows grace, is spoken of in the feminine gender.
1.9: 1.9 Let grace be added. To those who kept the law of the Lord, etc., down to for the grace of right working. And chains about your neck, etc. The brightness of perfect working, which confirms the preaching that proceeds through the neck, by the unfailing connection of virtues.
1.10: 1.10 My son. With a father's affection he addresses the son, coaxing him not to consent to sinners.
1.11: 1.11 Let us lie in wait. RABANUS. Either generally of robbers, who lay snares for the innocent. Or specially of those who delivered the author of life to death. STRABO. Since this pertains generally to all who lie in wait for blood, etc., down to and rather by presuming on themselves they destroy themselves. The innocent without cause. Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.
1.12: 1.12 Let us swallow him up alive as hell. Let us extinguish the memory of his virtues and doctrine, that he be not remembered even to have lived among us.
1.13: 1.13 We shall find all precious substance. Men, namely, whom they saw cleaving to Christ, whom they thought to separate from his love and company if they killed him, and to fill their houses with the spoils of such, that is, their conventicles with their souls.
1.14: 1.14 Cast in your lot among us. Of robbers generally it is plain, because to the companions they gather they promise a share of the prey; but also the persecutors of Christ joined to themselves whomever they could, those whom they saw following him they put out of the synagogue, that is, deprived them of their communion.
1.16: 1.16 They run to evil. Not only what they are going to do, but what they are going to suffer for what they have done. For the more they hasten to complete the crime, the nearer they draw to bear the punishment for the crime.
1.17: 1.17 In vain. RABANUS. The rest of the lying in wait specially for Christ, etc., down to for in the poor it has no cause.
1.20: 1.20 Wisdom. Hitherto the persecutions which the Jews inflicted on Christ; from here what he speaks after the passion to the same persecutors through the apostles. Wisdom, that is Christ, speaks without, that is in the light openly, that, infancy left behind, the little ones may be little in malice. RABANUS. For the Wisdom of God is Christ, etc., down to they should say to anyone. Without. THE SAME. Openly, after the resurrection, etc., down to: in the street his voice. In the streets he gives his voice, etc. What he had taught before a few, he plainly repeated, whence: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the light.
1.21: 1.21 At the head of multitudes he cries out, etc. THE SAME. Because even to the princes, who seemed to have prevailed against him that he be crucified, he openly recalled to memory the guilt of the homicide they had committed, and called them to the remedy of penance. In the entrance of the gates of the city. THE SAME. The city of the Lord, the Church gathered from both peoples, etc., down to he recalled to his grace; so that, as Luke says: A great multitude of the priests obeyed the faith, Acts 6.
1.22: 1.22 How long. You have already seen Christ in the flesh working miracles, whom you despised: now at least love him raised from death, and he will forgive what you have sinned. Little ones. RABANUS. The little ones are said to be slower in sense, etc., down to which the Son himself coming bestowed on those perfect in sense?
1.23: 1.23 Be converted. Wisdom exhorts to be converted to God, and brings forth the spirit. At my reproof. Through the apostles he rebukes the Jews, and admonishes them to be converted either after the ascension and resurrection.
1.26: 1.26 I also. THE SAME. Likewise in the psalm, etc., down to as if they would despise it as nothing.
1.27: 1.27 When sudden calamity shall fall. He speaks of the sudden siege of Jerusalem and the storming of the whole province by the Romans. Of which, Seeing the city, he wept over it, Luke 19. When it shall come upon you. RABANUS. This whole correction of wisdom can, etc., down to for what follows,
1.28: 1.28 They shall rise early and shall not find me, signifies the time of judgment, when some shall rise to life, others to everlasting reproach. They shall call upon. The Jews are not read to have called on the Lord in the siege; even if some called, because they did not truly repent, they were not heard.
1.29: 1.29 They hated. The just man on the contrary says: I hated the unjust, and loved your law.
1.31: 1.31 They shall eat therefore. THE SAME. Because they would not walk in my ways, etc., down to and it shall be well with you. And shall be filled with their own counsels. With which they said, etc., down to can be taken.
1.32: 1.32 The turning away. Turning away and prosperity destroys, when the mind turned from the fear of the Creator, and the wrath of the same Creator, seems to suffer nothing adverse in the things it sins in. But as Job says: They spend their days in good things, and in a moment go down to hell. Of the little ones. In sense, whence above, etc., down to but because they turn away, they kill themselves.
1.33: 1.33 But he that shall hear me shall rest without terror, etc. It can be understood in this life, and in the future, etc., down to he shall rest in the resurrection.
2.1: 2.1 My son. He notes two things here, that wisdom is of heavenly things, prudence of secular things. He hides the commandments of God with himself, etc., down to as seed cast by the wayside the birds carry away.
2.2: 2.2 Let your ear hear wisdom. He hears not with the ear, etc., down to for this is what follows: Incline your heart. Incline, humble, cleanse, etc., down to and have revealed them to the little ones. For if you shall call upon wisdom. To call upon, etc., down to nor ought free will to be absent.
2.4: 2.4 And dig for her as for treasures. He who digs for treasures, etc., down to nor rest until he find.
2.5: 2.5 Then shall you understand. The friendly fear, etc., down to but you will also find the knowledge of the Godhead itself which makes blessed forever.
2.6: 2.6 For the Lord gives. This verse looks back to what he had said above: For if you shall call upon wisdom, etc. For therefore wisdom, etc., down to but is given by the Lord. Out of his mouth. By the eternal birth of the Son, of which elsewhere: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before all creatures, Isaiah 58. Or, the mouth of the Lord in the saints, whence: The mouth of the Lord has spoken. And out of his mouth comes knowledge and prudence, while the Lord sanctifies the human mouth, and makes it his own, that it may speak knowingly and prudently.
2.7: 2.7 He will keep. That in whatever degree of virtue he may help the upright and simple. Job was simple and upright, Job 1.; simple, by the innocence of meekness, and upright, by the caution of discretion: simple, harming none, rather profiting all, upright, corrupted by none.
2.12: 2.12 From the evil way. To which they call who say: Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, he speaks perverse things who is the author of this persuasion.
2.13: 2.13 Who leave the right way. Beautifully, etc., down to his end is in the exterior darkness.
2.14: 2.14 Who are glad. Because they walk through dark ways, etc., down to and would chastise their harmful gladness with wholesome weeping.
2.16: 2.16 To deliver you from the strange woman. This verse depends, etc., down to: and they themselves are darts.
2.17: 2.17 And has forsaken the guide. It is plain also of the heretical mind, etc., down to which she had promised to keep on the day of baptism.
2.18: 2.18 Of her God, etc. What she pledged with her husband at the time of the wedding, the Lord being witness, that they would keep faith of chastity to each other, or in baptism. For her house is inclined. Every conversation of the adulteress leads to destruction, etc., down to that is, tends to the torments of the malignant spirits.
2.19: 2.19 None that go in to her shall return. Death, namely, not the woman, etc., down to let him not ascribe to himself, but to the grace of God.
2.21: 2.21 For they. Here he joins the simple to the upright, etc., down to they come to that which reigns with Christ in heaven.
2.22: 2.22 But the wicked. Of these it is said specially, etc., down to of the end of the good, but he who shall hear me shall rest without terror.
3.1: 3.1 My son, forget not. He teaches that works of mercy are to be pursued, etc., down to adorns with good deeds him whom he instructs.
3.2: 3.2 Peace, that is, the state of beatitude, etc., down to he would live a long time in the quiet of peace.
3.3: 3.3 Let not mercy and truth leave you. Let truth to be spoken never be absent from your mouth, mercy to be shown never from your work toward your neighbor: for so it comes about that the mercy of God also always follows you, which blots out sins; and the truth, which fulfills promises. Put them about your neck. In the throat is the organ of the voice, etc., down to nor let life contradict the voice.
3.4: 3.4 And you shall find grace. Before the Lord, etc., down to and may give to neighbors an example of living.
3.5: 3.5 Have confidence in the Lord. Fear not because of your weakness, etc., down to and what he has commanded, that you may be able to fulfill it, he will give. Be not wise. He seems to have said the same, etc., down to but what is the true wisdom of man he shows thus:
3.7: 3.7 Fear God and depart from evil. Such as is that in Job, etc., down to the memory of the divine fear restrains.
3.8: 3.8 For it shall be health. In the bones the solid works of virtues, etc., down to from which they may receive to be strengthened the more.
3.9: 3.9 Honor the Lord with your substance. That is, that men who are his hand, who were made to his image, may be recreated. And with the first of all your fruits. Not only of the substance of money, etc., down to he ascribes not to himself, but to him.
3.10: 3.10 And your barns shall be filled with abundance. Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven. If the saints have treasures in heaven, etc., down to by the heavenly remuneration is rendered. And your presses shall run over. Because the inward sweetness of eternal things kindles the hearts of all the faithful in the praise of their Creator. For here he says: That you may eat, etc.
3.11: 3.11 Instruction. There are those who serve the Lord in prosperity, etc., down to lose the piety which in tranquility he seemed to have.
3.12: 3.12 For whom the Lord loves he corrects. So much the less, etc., down to whence he himself says: Whom I love I rebuke and chastise.
3.13: 3.13 Blessed is the man, etc. Because those set under discipline, etc., down to and in the future to enjoy his vision. And he that abounds in prudence. Well, when he said, etc., down to to enlarge their hearts to receive its breadth.
3.14: 3.14 The purchase of it is better. Let him not fear the correction of poverty, whoever has acquired the riches of wisdom, for the heavenly gift surpasses all treasures. The first and purest. Because the root of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, these are the first and purest fruits, etc., down to is more perfectly promised by the Lord.
3.16: 3.16 Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left. By the vision of her divinity, etc., down to and in the future life everlasting.
3.17: 3.17 Her ways. Actions and doctrines, etc., down to pertain to examples of peace and love.
3.18: 3.18 She is a tree of life. As in the midst of paradise the tree of life, etc., down to he will be made blessed in the present sight.
3.19: 3.19 The Lord by wisdom. Typically, through the Son he placed the Church on the solidity of faith, he established the heavens by prudence, when through him he enlightened the hearts of lofty preachers.
3.20: 3.20 By his wisdom the depths broke out. In the days of Noah, etc., down to and show to the lesser ones as an example, they examine.
3.21: 3.21 My son, let them not depart. Lest, wearied by temporal discipline, you lose the grace of wisdom, which is so great, take heed.
3.22: 3.22 And there shall be life to your soul. Your soul has life with God, if you keep his decrees: although the flesh be pressed by the discipline of correction or even of death. And grace to your throat. The sense of the mind therefore has its throat, etc., down to: blessed is the man that hopes in him.
3.23: 3.23 Then shall you walk confidently. We walk confidently in our way, etc., down to for this is what follows: And your foot shall not stumble. Because to them that love God all things work together unto good, Romans 8.
3.24: 3.24 If you sleep, you shall not fear, you shall rest, and your sleep shall be sweet. It is plain according to the letter, etc., down to because he has God everywhere as protector and guardian.
3.27: 3.27 Do not withhold him from doing good who is able. Because above he diligently admonished to observe the law and counsel of the Lord, and promised eternal rest to those who observe, now in many ways he repeats what is to be observed. And first returning to what he had omitted, he teaches that mercy is to be shown to the neighbor, and that we must live justly with him. Then he forewarns that the enemy is to be guarded against. Do not therefore, he says, withhold. Lest you hear from the Lord with the Pharisees: You yourselves entered not in, and those who were entering in you hindered, Luke 11.
3.28: 3.28 Say not to your friend: Go, and come again, tomorrow I will give. Not only of alms, but of all the commandments of Christ, who says: You are my friends if you do the things I command you, John 15., etc.
3.30: 3.30 Strive not against a man without cause. He does not forbid striving against him who does evil, that he may be corrected, because this is not done in vain, which a certain necessity compels. Indeed he who says: If your brother shall sin against you, rebuke him, Matthew 18., himself wills that you bring back the erring one, as far as you can, to the way of truth.
3.32: 3.32 For every mocker is an abomination to the Lord. Every mocker, he says; because a mocker is one who either scorns to fulfill the words of God, which he knows, or corrupts them by perversely understanding and teaching. A mocker is also he who despises his promises as wicked, and spurns the wrath of his severity as tolerable. And also he who wickedly insults the simplicity of his neighbors. And so divine justice rightly abominates every such mocker. Well is it added: And his communication is with the simple, because the proud, while they mock the simple, judge themselves more prudent than those they deride. But their prudence, as James says, is earthly, sensual, devilish, James 3. The Lord's communication, however, is with the simple, because he enlightens with the secrets of wisdom those in whom he sees nothing of earthly pride and double-mindedness. Whence he says: You have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them to little ones, Luke 10.
3.33: 3.33 In the house of the wicked. As of the rich man in purple, who in this life lacked spiritual things, and afterward came to such want that he did not receive even a drop of water that he sought, whence: Who has blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ, who in the reward shall hear: Come, you blessed, Matthew 15., etc. But literally it often happens that those who plunder what is another's are at last consumed by want; but those who bestow their own abound even in earthly goods.
3.34: 3.34 The mockers. James and Peter placed these verses according to the old translation: Because God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble, James 4.
4.1: 4.1 Hear, children. From here, about to exhort to philosophy, he explains how he himself was taught wisdom by his father.
4.3: 4.3 For I also. Nothing raises minds more to the hope of obtaining wisdom than when we remember that those whom we admire as already shining in wisdom were once little and unlearned. Only one in the sight of my mother. But why does Solomon call himself the only one in the sight of his mother, when Scripture testifies that a uterine brother preceded him, except that that one, soon born, without a name, as if he had never been, departed from life?
4.4: 4.4 Let receive, etc. Such admonitions were given to Solomon by his father David: whoever rereads the Chronicles will find it.
4.5: 4.5 Get wisdom. In all that you possess, etc., down to in youth, having sold all, he bought.
4.9: 4.9 She shall give to your head. It is plain of Solomon, etc., down to and a crown besides of life will be given in the future.
4.10: 4.10 Hear, my son. Having set forth what he had received from his father, he returns to teaching the hearer the wisdom which he had begun.
4.11: 4.11 In the paths of equity. The paths, that is the actions of equity, etc., down to will be directed into the way of peace.
4.12: 4.12 And running. The more fully and eagerly you run to fulfill the commandments of God, the less you will fear adversities that may hinder you. For whoever sweat in wicked action find a stumbling block in the midst of their course, because suddenly, while they do not foresee, they are snatched to punishment.
4.17: 4.17 They eat the bread of wickedness. In the doing of crimes, etc., down to Scripture testifies.
4.18: 4.18 But the path of the just. The works of the just are carried out in the light of knowledge, and lead to eternal life, which is the perfect day.
4.19: 4.19 The way of the wicked. He says of these, etc., down to because running he shall not have a stumbling block.
4.20: 4.20 My son, hearken to my words. He admonishes to give ear to his words, and to withdraw from evil thoughts.
4.23: 4.23 With all watchfulness keep your heart. There are those who seem to men to live rightly, etc., down to the measure of life is estimated.
